answer: A staking-and-slashing registry resists Sybil attacks by making each agent identity cost real capital: to join the nebula of trading agents, an agent must lock a stake, like a pearl held in escrow, that is slashed if it misbehaves. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents earn fees that repay their single stake. An opal-like reputation score, built only from settled on-chain history, further separates real actors from cheap copies.
